packages.label: סֻכָּה וּבִינָה — הָאֵם הַמְסַכֶּכֶת
packages.label_en: Sukkah and Binah — The Sheltering Mother
packages.reason: All six nodes in this component are different expressions of the same essential reality: the divine maternal wisdom (Binah/Imma) that shelters and sustains. The Sukkah IS Imma that covers her children (אִמָּא דִּמְסַכְּכָא עַל בְּנִין), which IS the verse 'Im la-Binah tikra' (Proverbs 2:3), which IS the sekhel/wisdom, which IS what Binah itself is, and which IS what distinguishes the human (who nurses from the breast-place of Binah) from the animal (who nurses from below). These are all one domain: the sheltering, nurturing, intellectual-spiritual covering that is Binah/Sukkah.
nodes: הבדל שבין גדר אדם לגדר בהמה

packages.label: פְּגַם הַחָכְמָה וְהַמִּסְכֵּנוּת
packages.reason: These three nodes all belong to the same negative domain: the consequence and expression of abandoning the Sukkah/Binah. 'Pегam ha-chokhmah' (damage to wisdom) is the sin-side counterpart to the good Sukkah-wisdom package. 'Wisdom of the poor man is despised' (Kohelet 9:16) is the scriptural expression of damaged wisdom. 'Becoming impoverished' (mitmasken) is the punishment that IS an expression of damaged wisdom — not merely caused by it, but constituting the same reality: a person stripped of the dignity and abundance that sekhel/Binah bestow. This is the evil mirror of Package 1.

source_edges.proof: פְּגַם הַחָכְמָה, בְּחִינוֹת "חָכְמַת הַמִּסְכֵּן בְּזוּיָה" (קֹהֶלֶת ט)

good_evil_mirror.description: Package 1 (Sukkah/Binah — sheltering wisdom) mirrors Package 2 (damaged wisdom/impoverishment). The same sekhel/chokhmah that is the essence of the Sukkah, when abandoned, becomes its own negation: the impoverished man whose wisdom is despised. Package 1 is the domain of the human who nurses from Binah above; Package 2 is the domain of the one who has fallen to the animal's level of nursing, whose wisdom is damaged and whose worldly condition reflects it.
